CANONICAL_NAME.value: Mars Pathfinder priority inversion (1997) as Holzmann's Promela model, checked with SPIN 6.5.2

VERSION.value: Spin version-6.5.2 tarball, Examples/pathfinder.pml (same artifact as spin-6.5.2-holzmann)

ERA.value: 1997 (event); model in SPIN distributions since the 2000s

value.lineage: A REAL historical failure: the Mars Pathfinder lander (1997) suffered repeated system resets because a low-priority meteorological task held a mutex needed by the high-priority bus-management task while a medium-priority task starved it -- classic priority inversion under VxWorks, fixed by enabling priority inheritance. Holzmann's Promela model (Examples/pathfinder.pml in the SPIN distribution) reproduces the invalid end state (deadlock) and the fix. The failing model is preserved AS FAILING; SPIN is the instrument.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: real-time mutual exclusion across priority levels

value.built_to: share a resource between tasks of different priority on a real-time scheduler without the high-priority task being blocked indefinitely
value.pressure: hard deadlines (the watchdog resets the system), a shared bus with a mutex, three priority levels competing for the CPU
value.success_means: the high-priority task always gets the mutex within its deadline; the human record: without priority inheritance it did not, and the spacecraft reset

value.pressure: hard timing bounds, resource contention across priorities, a watchdog that treats delay as failure
value.failure_condition: priority inversion: the medium task runs, the low task holds the lock, the high task misses its deadline; the watchdog resets the lander

value: algorithm_from: Sha, Rajkumar, Lehoczky 1990 (the fix: priority inheritance)

evidence.ref: Glenn E. Reeves (JPL), What Really Happened on Mars Rover Pathfinder, 1997
evidence.says: Repeated spacecraft resets were caused by priority inversion: a low-priority task held a mutex needed by a high-priority task while a medium-priority task ran; the fix was to enable priority inheritance on that mutex.

evidence.ref: nyx/atlas/fingerprints/spin-pathfinder-priority-inversion-1997/ablate_rule_vs_mutex.json baseline: errors 1 at depth 4 (Nyx run, matches Techne)

cut.note: two processes, three shared variables, one guard clause: the whole body is smaller than this note

organs.human_interpretation: the low-priority task may run only while the high-priority task is idle (strict priority preemption)
organs.mechanism: every transition of one process is guarded by a predicate over ANOTHER process's state variable; the guarded process is ineligible to take any step -- including the step that would release a resource -- whenever the predicate is false
organs.output: eligibility of every step of the guarded process
assumptions: the high process's 'waiting' state is NOT idle -- a waiting high task keeps the low task frozen
organs.interface: a Promela `provided` clause; in a real RTOS, the scheduler's ready-queue policy
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: encodes the lander's fixed-priority scheduler in one clause
organs.failure_landscape: with a resource held by the frozen process: deadlock (measured)
organs.ablation: REMOVE (A1): errors 1 -> 0. REVERSE (A3): 0. WEAKEN so that waiting counts as yielding (A4): 0. The deadlock needs this rule AND needs 'waiting' to count as not-idle.
organs.human_prior: named 'scheduling rule' by the model's own comment
organs.control: CONTROL_rename_constants: identical model, renamed constants -> errors 1 (the verifier is not keying on names)
organs.cheat: none identified: exhaustive search over 12 states
organs.observability: pan reports depth and errors; trail replays the schedule
organs.intervention_readiness: YES -- one-line edits, 1.5 s per verification

organs.human_interpretation: a lock: wait until free, then take it, in one indivisible step
organs.mechanism: a guard on a shared variable and the assignment that falsifies the guard are fused into one atomic step, so two processes cannot both pass; release is a plain assignment back
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: protects the shared data buffer between producer and consumer
organs.failure_landscape: held by a process that cannot run: everyone else waiting on it is stuck (measured with the rule present)
organs.ablation: REMOVE the guard (A2, `skip`): errors 1 -> 0 -- the deadlock also needs the lock; mutual exclusion is lost (not measured)
organs.human_prior: 'mutex' is the model's own variable name
organs.observability: mutex variable is `show`n in the trail

rejected_cuts.evidence: record.behavioral_entry_point says 'toggle the priority-inheritance option in pathfinder.pml'; the file contains no such option, no #ifdef, no second mode; Techne's own recipe toggles nothing and verifies the model as-is
rejected_cuts.note: TECHNE FEEDBACK: the record names a switch the body does not have. The fix humans applied on Mars (enable priority inheritance on the mutex) is NOT in this fossil; a repaired model would be a separate specimen

rejected_cuts.candidate: the medium-priority task of the Pathfinder story
rejected_cuts.evidence: the human account needs three tasks (low holds, medium preempts, high starves); the model has TWO processes and deadlocks anyway, because `provided (h_state == idle)` freezes low whenever high is merely waiting. A4 shows the deadlock vanishes when waiting counts as idle.
rejected_cuts.note: the model's rule over-approximates: it stands in for the medium task by treating a blocked high task as if it still occupied the CPU. Famous-name vs body divergence, recorded as a surprise

rejected_cuts.candidate: the SPIN verifier (state-space search, partial-order reduction, trail replay)
rejected_cuts.evidence: present in the same tarball and built by the recipe, but it is the INSTRUMENT that observes the model, not machinery of the specimen; it is the fossil spin-6.5.2-holzmann
l_state is written and never read by any guard; h_state is read only by the rule organ. l_state is display state for the trail (`show`), not machinery
rejected_cuts.note: half of the model's declared state does not participate in any transition

pressures.condition: tasks of different urgency share one resource that must be held exclusively; the urgent task must complete within a bound; a watchdog treats lateness as failure
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one exclusive resource + CPU time ordered by priority
pressures.failure_condition: the urgent task waits on the resource while its holder is not permitted to run
pressures.world_punishes: a missed deadline (the lander reset itself repeatedly)
pressures.world_rewards: the urgent task getting the resource within its bound, regardless of who holds it
pressures.observable_consequence: a schedule with no enabled step (pan: invalid end state at depth 4)
pressures.vacuity_condition: a single priority level, or no shared resource
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: give everything the same priority (loses the timing guarantee the priorities exist for)
pressures.cheat_control: the CONTROL variant (renamed constants) still deadlocks; A1-A4 each remove the deadlock by removing a real precondition
pressures.cost_class: 12 reachable states; the failure is structural, not statistical
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: a spacecraft computer that shares a bus-data structure between a fast task and a slow task
